scope: Read-only status, stage, and host-capacity estimate; no worker changes.

evidence.prepared_runtime_policy: README documents eight single-thread CPU workers; source checks worker index against prepared workers and assigns static round-robin priority schedule.

eta.estimate_basis: 0.50 ps logged in window_001 heating over elapsed wall time since process start; early heating only, stage mtime used as timing endpoint.
eta.uncertainty: Very high: rate comes from only the first 0.5 ps of heating; temperature gate is 25–350 K for heating and 250–350 K for later stages; stage transitions, equilibration/production throughput, I/O, failures/retries, and contention may change rate. These are nominal elapsed estimates, not validated completion forecasts.

capacity.observed_other_competing_work: Two GPU pmemd processes, at least five separate sander NEB processes, two Gaussian l502 processes consuming about four logical CPUs each, plus CPU-heavy monitors; process sample showed each of the eight US sander workers at ~100%.
capacity.safe_headroom_assessment: No defensible spare physical-core headroom at this snapshot: load average exceeds 24 physical cores and eight US workers already saturate eight cores. Do not infer that RAM availability implies CPU capacity. Reassess after competing NEB/Gaussian work changes.
capacity.worker_limit_context: Prepared config and README set eight single-thread workers; runtime enforces configured index range and round-robin queues. No evidence for increasing that prepared limit in this audit.

assumptions: 36 ps/window = 1 ps heating + 5 ps equilibration + six 5 ps production blocks.
11 ps/window for a first 5 ps production receipt = 1 ps heating + 5 ps equilibration + first 5 ps production block.
Idealized queue makespan assumes uniform throughput across all stages and all workers; it excludes transition overhead and retries.
